findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, so the feature flag has no effect
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`, returns false if enabled, and then returns false unconditionally. The result is that SQL expressions are disabled regardless of the flag. The logic is confusing and suggests a half-finished edit. If the intent is a hard kill switch, the function should simply return false with a comment saying so, and the feature-flag lookup should be removed. As written, a maintainer reading the flag check would believe the flag gates the feature.

findings.title: The SQL gate is only in the reader; NewSQLCommand and UnmarshalSQLCommand have no gate
findings.body: The disable check lives only in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery. `UnmarshalSQLCommand` in sql_command.go calls `NewSQLCommand` directly and never checks the gate. Any other caller that builds an SQL command bypasses the disable. It currently fails only because the stubbed `sql.TablesList` always returns an error. That is incidental, not a guard, so a future change to the DB stub would reopen the vulnerability. The check should be enforced in `NewSQLCommand` or at the execution boundary.

findings.title: Error message says 'not implemented' for a deliberate security disable
findings.body: Users who enable sqlExpressions will get 'sqlExpressions is not implemented', which misstates the situation. The message should say the feature is disabled for security reasons and point to the advisory. Operators trying to diagnose it will be misled.

findings.title: Stub DB makes every SQL expression fail, including legitimate ones
findings.body: TablesList, RunCommands and QueryFramesInto all return 'not implemented'. Because `sql.TablesList` in parser.go depends on RunCommands, `NewSQLCommand` now fails for every query. The SQL expression type is therefore completely non-functional, not just locked down. This is a deliberate hotfix, but nothing in the PR documents that the feature is gutted, and the stubbed DB type is named as if it were a real in-memory database. This should be an explicit, documented temporary state.

findings.title: Quote-escaping is still used to build SQL via fmt.Sprintf
findings.body: TablesList still interpolates user SQL into a string with fmt.Sprintf after only doubling single quotes. This is the injection-prone pattern that the RCE/LFI issue is about. It is currently unreachable because RunCommands is stubbed, but it will be dangerous as soon as a real engine is reconnected. Keeping this code path unchanged in a security fix is risky.

findings.title: tablesFromAST indexes ast[0] without checking length
findings.body: `flatten.Flatten(ast[0], ...)` panics if the slice is empty, for example if the JSON decodes to `[]`. The code is unreachable today, but the panic would become reachable as soon as the stub is replaced.

findings.title: No tests added for the disabled SQL path
findings.body: The PR changes the reader's behaviour for QueryTypeSQL and removes a dependency, but adds no test asserting that SQL expression queries are rejected. A regression test is needed so that the gate cannot be silently removed, and a test for UnmarshalSQLCommand to confirm the bypass is closed.
